newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka blood banks short of stock as offensive begins.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka blood banks short of stock as offensive begins.

text.p: Sri Lanka's biggest blood bank has called for urgent blood donations as stocks run low after the military launched its latest offensive against Tamil rebels, the independent Island newspaper said.
The newspaper said on Friday that the Central Blood Bank at Colombo's National Hospital, was running low on blood as demand from the military had increased in the past few days.
It said the military was taking 50-60 pints of blood daily to the base hospital in Anuradhapura, 170 km (106.25 miles) northeast of capital Colombo, to treat soldiers wounded in the offensive.
The blood bank's stock, normally around 1,000 pints, was down to 500 pints, it added.

Sri Lankan troops launched a fresh offensive against the rebel Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) on Tuesday and the defence ministry said on Thursday that army casualities in the four-day offensive stood at 18 dead and 31 wounded.
Health officials were not immediately available for comment.

The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
